evidence.reason: The test `test_new_image_must_match_the_refreshed_manifest` exists to prove fetch_image verifies new downloads against the refreshed remote manifest rather than a stale local one. In the current code (lines 435-443) the stale manifest is `"2"*64`, the refreshed manifest is `"3"*64`, and the downloaded bytes are `b"unexpected"`. Since both checksums differ from sha256(b"unexpected"), a buggy implementation that ignores the refresh and verifies against the stale checksum still raises ValueError and still leaves no image — so the test passes either way and cannot detect the regression it names. This is a genuine test-correctness defect (routine repair, no owner decision). Fixing by writing vm.sha256_bytes(b"unexpected") into the stale manifest makes stale usage verify successfully and promote the image, causing the expected ValueError/absence assertions to fail as intended, while keeping the refreshed checksum different preserves the positive path. The issue is still present at the current tip.
